Phase 1 First-in-Human study results demonstrating etalanetug safety and target engagement in healthy subjects

evidence_assessment: Clinical evidence for the anti-tau monoclonal antibody etalanetug (E2814) is currently limited to Phase 1 data, which has demonstrated an adequate safety profile and robust target engagement in both healthy volunteers and participants with dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease (DIAD). Early open-label data from a DIAD cohort showed etalanetug robustly reduced CSF MTBR-tau243 by up to 71.6% and ptau217 by 57.9%, alongside stabilization of tau PET signals over 108 weeks. The safety and efficacy of combining etalanetug with the FDA-approved anti-amyloid drug lecanemab, which the analyzed document focuses on, are currently being evaluated in this Phase 2 trial (NCT06602258) and in the parallel DIAN-TU tau platform trial (NCT05269394). Because no results from these dual-therapy combination trials have been published yet, the central claim that etalanetug with lecanemab provides dose-dependent biomarker efficacy remains a clinical hypothesis awaiting validation.
